lines.before: **"Green" = every step of every CI workflow file**, not a remembered subset - or name the skipped step and why. Before a PR run the tests covering the change, however small; CI's run on the push is the gate (no CI, or none on the PR: the full suite once locally) - "reasoned unaffected" is not "ran it green"; copy each command from a full read of the workflow (a folded run block is one command); the exit code is the gate - echo it, never filter output through an invented pattern; re-run the dependency audit before the PR and before merge commands. A test runner may reuse a server already on its port and test a stale build - check who owns it, never kill the owner's. Why: a remembered subset is how red mains happen. <!-- PROJECT ADAPTER A9/A10 -->

lines.before: Size a test by what it needs, not its type: **small** (one process), **medium** (this machine), **large** (another machine, a real service, a browser, a live model); ask before writing it. Large tests live in the slow-lane folder (`tests/slow`, or `.kit/lanes.json`). Two lanes on one PR, both required to merge: the fast lane reports first; the slow lane runs beside it, on by a job-level `if` when its folder holds a test, never a path filter. `node .claude/lane-state.mjs` reports one lane, two lanes or over budget (fast lane over its budget, default 10 minutes, 3 PR runs in a row); then the levers in order: measure, parallel, cancel stale runs, change-scoped selection, and moving a test to the slow lane last. A fast test over its limit (300 s) fails: fix or move it, with the reason. A bug the slow lane catches gets a fast test before its fix. The owner's alone: a lane leaving the merge decision. A security or owner-rule test never changes lane for speed. Model-calling evals run in their own lane against the owner's threshold. **CI shape:** `_Templates/ci-<stack>.yml`; gaps: `node .claude/ci-shape.mjs`. pytest: mark by folder in a `conftest.py` hook, markers registered, `--strict-markers`. Why: fast feedback without lowering the gate.

lines.before: **Terms:** "the owner" = the human who owns the project and locks decisions. "Claude" / "the lead" = the AI session doing the work. "The vault" = the governance `.md` files (tracking files, specs, plans, ADRs), often gitignored. "Tracked" = committed to git. "The owner's yes" = the owner's Yes in a choice pop-up quoting the act exactly. "Outward act" = an act that leaves the machine (push, PR, merge, release, tag, public post, a message out). "The push bound" = the one push that needs no yes (rule:outward-acts). "Gate bypass" = switching a check off (skipping the git hooks, moving the hooks path). "Protected file" = a file only install or the owner writes (the guards, git hooks, .git/config, the settings, the session transcripts).

lines.why: Build 11 recall: 14 of 20 answers to "Can I push and open the PR?" left out that the PR needs no yes; the push bound now names the PR in its definition, and an answer about pushing or a PR names both acts

lines.before: - **The push bound** (the owner, 2026-11-10) is the one push that needs no yes: `git push [-u] origin <feature branch>`. It has four limits, and an answer about pushing names all four: never main, never a tag, never a force, never a delete. Main takes a PR; a tool pushes there only as a new repo's first push, with the owner's yes. Opening the PR from that feature branch (`gh pr create`, on that repo) needs no yes either (the owner, 2026-11-15): do it, then tell the owner.
lines.after: - **The push bound** (the owner, 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-15) is the push and the PR that need no yes: `git push [-u] origin <feature branch>`, then opening that branch's PR (`gh pr create`, on that repo); do them, then tell the owner. It has four limits, and an answer about pushing or a PR names both acts and all four limits: never main, never a tag, never a force, never a delete. Main takes a PR; a tool pushes there only as a new repo's first push, with the owner's yes.
